properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 11 at 8:07AM EDT until October 11 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Wilmington NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to one half foot of
inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Horry and Coastal Georgetown Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 10 AM EDT this
morning. For the High Rip Current Risk, until 8 PM EDT this
evening.

* IMPACTS...Vulnerable causeways to and from local beaches may
experience minor coastal flooding. Low-lying roads and
locations along the Intracoastal Waterway and adjacent tidal
creeks may observe minor coastal flooding. Check with local
officials for the latest information regarding coastal flood
impacts and closures. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Affected areas listed are based on
average tide conditions. Additional locations may experience
flooding during periods of heavy rainfall, high winds, or
other factors.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

California...

properties.headline: Tropical Cyclone Local Statement issued October 11 at 3:18AM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
HLSSGX

This product covers EXTREME SOUTHWESTERN CALIFORNIA

**THE REMNANTS OF RACHEL CONTINUE TO BRING HEAVY RAINS AND GUSTY WINDS
TO PORTIONS OF BAJA CALIFORNIA AND THE SOUTHWESTERN UNITED STATES**

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- All watches and warnings have been canceled

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 90 miles east-southeast of San Mateo Point CA or about 60
miles east-northeast of Mouth of Tijuana River CA
- 32.9N 116.1W
- Storm Intensity 50 mph
- Movement North or 10 degrees at 25 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Impacts from Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel Occurred in San Diego this
morning and could continue into the early afternoon.

Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel is currently about 60 miles east
northeast of San Diego, moving north at about 25 mph. Rachel no longer
has tropical characteristics and tropical storm level impacts will
diminish in San Diego County this morning. The Tropical Storm Watch
has been cancelled for all of San Diego County. Coastal flooding,
wind, and periods of heavy rain which could lead to localized flooding
and flash flooding will continue to be a concern today. The majority
of impacts from the tropical storm have ended.

South swell from Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel will continue today. The
combination of south and northwest swells, increased onshore winds,
and high tides over 7 feet will maintain a threat of coastal flooding
and beach erosion along area beaches. Surf today is currently expected
to peak at 6 to 9 feet, decreasing to 3 to 6 feet for Monday and
Tuesday. Confidence in impactful coastal flooding is high, with
significant coastal flooding and beach erosion likely.

Widespread rain from Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel will decrease
through today. There is a gradient in rainfall amounts with the higher
amounts over San Diego County, the mountains, and parts of the low
desert. Peak rainfall rates of 0.50 to 0.80 inches were observed for
the coast and valleys, 0.50 to 0.70 inches per hour in the deserts,
and 0.70 to 1 inch per hour in the mountains. Observed rainfall totals
so far are as follows: 0.48-0.95 inches in the San Diego County
coastal areas, 0.55-2.37 for the San Diego County valleys,
0.32-2.15 for the San Diego County mountains and 0.76-1.57 for the San
Diego County deserts. Areas of flash and urban flooding occurred. The
San Diego River at Fashion Valley is currently forecast to crest at
8.1 feet (action/monitor stage) just before noon today. Those with
interests near the San Diego River should continue to monitor the
forecast.

Increased winds occurred with the onset and passage of Post-Tropical
Cyclone Rachel. Sustained winds of 59 mph were observed and stronger
wind gusts were associated with thunderstorms. The southern and
eastern parts of San Diego County saw winds of this magnitude,
although strong sustained winds and wind gusts also occurred
elsewhere. Winds were enhanced by local terrain. Winds are expected to
remain elevated in Rachel's wake with continued strong gusts on the
desert mountain slopes into the deserts through Monday morning.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* WIND:
Little to no additional wind impacts expected.

- Community officials are now assessing the extent of actual wind
impacts accordingly.
- Emergency response teams are attending to casualty situations
as needed.
- Emergency work crews are restoring essential community
infrastructure as necessary.
- If you have an emergency dial 9 1 1.


* SURGE:
Little to no additional surge impacts expected.

- Community officials are now assessing the extent of actual
surge impacts accordingly.
- Emergency response teams are attending to casualty situations
as needed.
- Emergency work crews are restoring essential community
infrastructure as necessary.
- If you have an emergency dial 9 1 1.


Elsewhere across EXTREME SOUTHWESTERN CALIFORNIA, little to no impact
is anticipated.

* FLOODING RAIN:
Additional impacts from flooding rain are still a concern across San
Diego County. Remain well guarded against dangerous flood waters
having further impacts of significant potential.

Additional impacts from flooding rain are still a concern across San
Diego County. Remain well guarded against locally hazardous flood
waters having further impacts of limited potential.

* TORNADOES:
Little to no impacts are anticipated at this time across EXTREME
SOUTHWESTERN CALIFORNIA.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials.

* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:
Remain safely sheltered until conditions improve. When going outside
be sure to stay away from downed power lines, hazardous debris and
flooded areas.

If your home or shelter was damaged, be alert to the smell of gas
leaks and be cautious around electrical wiring, broken glass, jagged
metal and wood, and protruding nails and screws.

Check to see if everyone in your group is OK. Administer first aid to
those who are injured. If possible, call 9 1 1 for any serious
injuries. Remember, it may be difficult for emergency responders to
arrive quickly.

Check in with your emergency points of contact. Let them know your
location and status. Keep conversations short and to the point. Do
not tie up communications systems.

Check on your neighbors. If necessary, help them connect with their
points of contact.

Do not attempt to return to evacuated areas until local authorities
have inspected roads and bridges and have given the all clear.
Hazards like downed power lines and trees, washed out roads,
continued flooding in low lying areas and non-functioning traffic
lights make travel difficult.

Allow extra time for emergency vehicles to reach you as they navigate
road hazards.

Do not attempt to return to evacuated areas until local authorities
give the all clear. Allow time for officials to inspect bridges and
overpasses and to mark washed-out roads.

When entering areas that have been heavily damaged, bring along a
GPS-enabled device to help with street navigation. Do not drive on
roads that have been marked closed.

Do not go sightseeing within impacted communities. Sightseers
interfere with the emergency work of first responders.

When inspecting damage, use flashlights rather than candles or flamed
lanterns. Be aware of sparks that can ignite natural gas or other
leaking flammables.

Do not go up on your roof until the weather conditions are safe.
Ladders can be slippery in the rain and unexpected wind gusts can
blow you off the roof.

When clearing out fallen trees, be careful with chainsaws and axes.
Always wear protective gear and keep others at a safe distance.
Leaning trees and those which have fallen on roofs or power lines can
be especially dangerous. If you are not in good health or unsure
about what you are doing, have someone with tree cutting experience
do the job. Never cut trees without a partner.

If using a generator, avoid carbon monoxide poisoning by following
instructions provided by the manufacturer. Operate your generator in
a well-ventilated space outside of your living area and away from
open doors and windows.

Problems with sewer backups can further contaminate standing flood
waters. Keep children away from flood waters. Also, listen for boil
water alerts as tap water may have become non-potable.

Be alert for any lingering wind gusts which could take down weakened
trees and/or power lines, collapse damaged structures, or cause
flying debris.

Be alert for potential flooding from rising rivers and streams which
may have yet to crest. Remain informed of the latest river forecasts
and heed any flood watches and warnings.

Be alert for flooded roads which could be compromised or littered
with debris. Avoid travel until water levels subside and roads have
been cleared. Do not drive through places where flood waters cover
the road. Turn around, don't drown!

Have multiple ways to receive Tornado Warnings if issued. Consider
nearby shelter options as you move about. Be ready to shelter quickly.

* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in San Diego CA around 8 AM PDT, or sooner if conditions
warrant.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Eastern Caldwell County in western North Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 945 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low-lying areas adjacent to streams
and other poor-drainage areas, including farmland, parks,
greenways, boat-access areas, golf courses, underpasses, and
parking lots. Isolated, shallow flows over roadways is possible. A
few flood-prone, low-water crossings may become impassible. A small
culvert washout or two is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 339 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated a round of moderate
rainfall recently has departed eastern Caldwell County, with
additional cells of moderate rainfall moving into the county from
the south.  This rainfall is occurring on top of saturated soils
resulting from a prolonged period of light to moderate showers
that occurred over the county yesterday. Storm-total rainfall of
2.5 to 4.5 inches has been observed across eastern Caldwell
County since yesterday, with the highest totals from Cajah's
Mountain to Sawmills and Granite Falls.  Areas streams have been
steadily rising in response to this heavy rainfall and isolated,
out-of-bank conditions impacting low-lying areas adjacent to
streams are likely to develop over the next 1-3 hours.

Areas of greatest concern include along Lower Creek in Lenoir,
where a streamgauge on Harrisburg Dr is at 8.53 feet and
approaching the Action/Advisory Stage of 9.0 feet. At 9.0 feet,
flooding of low-lying, undeveloped woodland surrounding Lenoir
Mall will begin.

- Additional rounds of showers and thunderstorms may develop
through 9am this morning.  These showers and storms will be very
efficient at producing heavy rainfall.  Soils are saturated and
streams are swollen. Therefore, additional heavy rain may quickly
create new areas of flooding and cause previous areas of flooding
to redevelop.  As a result, a Flash Flood Warning may be issued
this morning.  Caution is advised near any stream or other
vulnerable area.  Seek higher ground immediately if heavy rain
develops.  Please have a plan in place should flash flooding
develop and do not hesitate to act.  Please heed all evacuation
orders from Emergency Management officials.

- Some locations that may experience flooding include...
Hickory, Lenoir, Sawmills, Granite Falls, Gamewell, Hudson,
Cajah's Mountain, Rhodhiss, and Cedar Rock.

- Https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:
ESFPPG

An active trough to the north is projected to drift southward and
move over the territory by early or midweek. This trough should
remain strong and active while over the territory, and may even
intensify with embedded low pressure centers. Widespread showers
may be heavy and persistent at times with the possibility of
thunderstorms. Widespread flash flooding may occur from this
rainfall, and landslides will be possible along steep mountainous
terrain. Impacts could begin as early as Tuesday and are expected
to persist through the weekend. While there is still uncertainty
in the exact magnitude and duration of rainfall, plan now for wet
conditions that could start as early as Tuesday and persist
through at least Sunday.

Keep up to date with the latest forecast information through our
internet page (www.weather.gov/ppg), local media, social media,
and our NOAA Radio broadcasts.

* WHERE...Northern Greenville County in upstate South Carolina...

top of saturated soils due to a prolonged period of light to
moderate showers that have occurred over the county since this
morning.  Widespread, storm-total rainfall of the 2.5-3.5 inches

North Tyger rivers from Tigerville to Gowensville.  Isolated to
scattered out-of-bank conditions impacting low-lying areas
adjacent to streams are likely to develop over the next 1-3
hours.

tonight and the threat will persist through the early morning
hours on Sunday.  These showers and storms will be very efficient
at producing heavy rainfall.  Soils are saturated and streams are
swollen. Therefore, additional heavy rain may quickly create new
areas of flooding and cause previous areas of flooding to
redevelop.  As a result, Flash Flood Warnings may be issued
tonight.  Caution is advised near any stream or other vulnerable
area.  Seek higher ground immediately if heavy rain develops.

Emergency Management officials.

Park, Jones Gap State Park, Caesars Head State Park, Table Rock

Tropical Storm Rachel over the San Diego River basin is expected
tonight into late Sunday morning. The San Diego River at Fashion
Valley is expected to peak at 8.1 ft (action/monitor stage) just
before Noon on Sunday, falling below action stage Sunday afternoon.

* WHERE...San Diego River at Fashion Valley.

* WHEN...For Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 7.5 feet, Action stage. The first real impacts are
seen on the San Diego River at this level. Low lying roads in and
around Fashion Valley Mall begin to take on water. Avenida Del Rio
is the first road to begin flooding.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:15 PM PDT Saturday the stage was 2.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 10.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 8.1 feet
late tomorrow morning.
- Action stage is 7.5 feet.
- Flood stage is 10.0 feet.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:
* WHAT...DAMAGING sea-water coastal flooding is likely through
Sunday, especially near the Sunday morning high tide where
anticipated tide levels are expected to be around 8 feet. The
most likely areas for DAMAGING coastal flooding on Sunday
morning will be vulnerable south-facing beaches due to the
expected combination of very high level tide levels around 8
feet (including additive effect of low barometric pressure and
onshore winds gusting to 15 to 25 mph), high surf of 5 to 8
feet, and light to moderate rainfall. For all other beaches,
minor to moderate coastal flooding is expected near times of
high tide. From Sunday night through Tuesday, there will be the
continued threat of at least minor to moderate coastal flooding

south facing shores. Dangerous rip currents are likely.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 3 PM PDT Sunday.
For the High Surf Advisory, from 6 AM to 10 PM PDT Sunday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 PM Sunday to 2 PM PDT
Tuesday.

Peninsula and Naples in Long Beach as well as Malibu),
SIGNIFICANT sea- water flooding will likely DAMAGE coastal
structures and beach roadways around the time of high tide,
especially the Sunday morning high tide. In addition,
significant ponding of water on low-lying beach roadways could
make driving difficult. THERE IS GROWING CONFIDENCE THAT THE
EXPECTED COASTAL FLOODING IMPACTS ON SUNDAY MORNING FOR
VULNERABLE SOUTH FACING BEACHES OF LA COUNTY COULD BE THE MOST
SIGNIFICANT WE HAVE SEEN SO FAR THIS SEASON, INCLUDING THOSE
SEEN WITH MARIE. For all other beaches and harbors, shallow with
minor to moderate sea- water flooding will likely impact
beaches and walkways, especially with the Sunday morning high
tide which could cause local damage to most vulnerable locations
such as Venice. For all beach areas, significant erosion is
expected. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning.
Dangerous and life- threatening rip currents can pull swimmers
and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury,
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near
shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides of around 8 feet are expected on
Sunday morning (nearly 2 feet above astronomical high tide of
6.1 feet), returning to around 7.5 feet for Monday and Tuesday
mornings. The projected high tides of around 8 feet for Sunday
morning would approach or exceed recent record tide levels for
LA county. Large secondary high tides are also expected each
evening.

Stay off of beaches and coastal walkways, roads, and structures.
Do NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued October 10 at 9:31AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...The Imperial County APCD has issued an air quality alert
due to harmful levels of particle pollution from windblown dust.
Visit https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted
air quality levels.

* WHERE...the Imperial Valley. Levels of particle pollution can vary
by time and location depending on emissions and local weather
conditions.

* WHEN...Sunday, October 11, 2026 from 12:00 AM until 10:00 PM.

* IMPACTS... Particle pollution can get deep into the lungs and
cause serious health problems such as asthma attacks, heart and lung
disease symptoms, and increased risk of lung infections. Everyone
can be affected, but sensitive groups such as people with lung or
heart disease, older adults, people who are pregnant, children, and
those who spend a lot of time outdoors are at greater risk.
properties.instruction:
To protect your health, check air quality levels and act as needed:

* When Air Quality Index (AQI) levels are "Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups" (orange), sensitive groups as specified
above should limit extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Unhealthy" (red), everyone may experience health
impacts. Sensitive groups should avoid extended time outdoors.
* When AQI is "Very Unhealthy" (purple), sensitive groups should
avoid all outdoor physical activity. Everyone else should
avoid extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Hazardous" (maroon), everyone should avoid all
outdoor physical activity.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

To help keep indoor air clean when air quality is poor:

* Keep windows and doors closed
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, grilling, and gasoline-powered lawn and garden
equipment

To help minimize outdoor particle pollution levels:

* Carpool, telecommute, reduce trips, or take public
transportation
* Slow down if driving on dirt roads
* Stabilize loose soils
